a.text: Hibiscus and I will be on the way to see you by the time you get this letter. No point writing to try and turn us back, we won't get it anyway.
I know you don't want to admit it yourselves, but I know why you had to move again in such a rush.
I know you say the fighting's long passed and your village is nice and remote and the villagers are all fairly tolerant of Sarkaz, but does that really describe anywhere in Victoria anymore?

Besides, according to you, everything's been just hunky-dory ever since the war in Londinium broke out. That's why we have to come see for ourselves if you're doing as fine as you say you are. If anyone's giving you trouble.
Point being, we can talk when we meet. Promise me you'll look after yourselves.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava, you found the chili powder yet? We're not gonna make it in time for dinner if we don't start marinating the meat soon...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Stop rushing me. We only need to get it done before they're home. Why's so much of their stuff in boxes...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: A harp? I didn't know they learned music.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's their friend's. The really good one, Mr. Baroque. I think they lost all contact with him after the war broke out.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...Eurgh, they've still got our workbooks from primary school! I think we should just toss these...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You can't do that! We're almost never home. Mum likes to flip through them.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Flip through these? It's not like we never visit... here's a pile of photo albums—oof! Heavy!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Are these... all from when they were working in Londinium? I don't recognize any of these people... I think by the clothes, it's all their coworkers. Every photo in here has been kept like brand new.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And under that are all the letters. Honestly, you'd think after moving so many times they'd have thrown these away... nothing but clutter.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: This pretty much represents most of Mum and Dad's life, after all... we're not going to get it organized just like that. Could you ask anyone to sort out their entire life that easily?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Not to mention they have to head out for work during the day...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Not in here—not in here... maybe the shelves? Urk...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...Hibiscus, look at this.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: These are recruitment notices... typist, gardener, childcarer... crossed out, all of them.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: They used to work as engineers...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Is living in Victoria really worth putting up with this...?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If you make them leave, where else can they go?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava, put those notices back. And don't bring it up in front of them. We should just... focus on doing what we can.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...Can't find the chili powder. I'll ask the neighbors if I can borrow some.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Wait—oh, she's just going to storm off like that... I needed to warn her not to get into rows with the neighbors...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hello, I live in the building furthest on the east. Would it be any trouble if I borrowed...

steps.name: Neighbor A
steps.text: Er... no, sorry, we don't have any. Best of luck.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Won't even hear me finishing a sentence...)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hello, I'm wondering if I could borrow some chili powder.
They flatly shut the door in her face.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Tolerant... you say?)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hello, I'm living in...

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Um...
A curious child peeks out from behind her mother's back, peeking at the young Sarkaz girl at their door.

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: Ilsa, back in your room.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: We only just moved in not long ago...

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: I know. You've been knocking on every door before mine. Got something the matter?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: My sister's making dinner, and we can't find where the chili powder went. Could we borrow a bit?

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: ...So that's all, is it? Wait there a sec if you please.
The door closes, only to then creak ajar. Out peeks an inquisitive little head that stares at Lava—or more precisely, at the horns on her head.
The girl gulps somewhat anxiously, dithers for a moment, then reaches out a hand to Lava.
Lava is well inured to being looked at this way by now, and doesn't twitch. Bit by bit the girl's miniature hand reaches close, and touches on the corner of Lava's hem.

steps.name: Curious Girl
steps.text: Wow—it's real clothes. Not witchcrafty ones.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Excuse me?

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: Ilsa! Get back here now!
The mother drops what she was holding, runs to the door, and shields her child behind her. The calm has fled her face. It was bound to.

steps.name: Neighbor B
steps.text: We don't have what you're looking for. You can move along.

With a furtive rustle, Ilsa climbs out the loft window and excitedly sends the sign to her friends. Soon, more and more people in the street are coming to a standstill as they spot a strange scene unfolding in the distance—
An unwelcome Sarkaz with a chilly expression walking through their village, and a gaggle of children tiptoeing not far behind her.
The lot of them duck behind bushes, dodge behind trees, wink and signal to each other, and occasionally talk into imaginary walkie-talkies in their hands.

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Reporting in. The devil's at the haypile in front of Tom's place. She's about to reach his front door. Over!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Roger that! Defense artillery is in place!

steps.name: Concerned Passerby
steps.text: Mind, children, you oughtn't catapult things at her. You'll be putting yourselves in great danger...
At an adult's intervention, the children squawk like fowlbeasts and scatter, only to gather again soon after.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Tch. Listen, you lot...

steps.name: Children
steps.text: The devil's spotted us! Evacuate!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Devil...?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (What a pain. I need to just scare them off.)

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Everyone, look, there's all shiny footprints down the street she went. What's that about?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Hold on, I'm gonna check it out—whoa, whoa, giddy up, it's all fire! Wherever she walks, it's catching fire!

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Lemme see—it is! All these footprints are lit on fire! That's amazing!

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Hey, she's getting out of sight! After her!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (What, still not enough to scare you?)
Lava stares briefly at the catapults in their hands.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hmph, fine. It'd be more hassle if I got any of you hurt. Try this on for size, then.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Ah-choo—

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: She just sneezed fire! Whoa, now she's got all fire wings!

steps.name: Ilsa & Rose
steps.text: Wowww—! So...

steps.name: Ilsa & Rose
steps.text: So cool!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...Okay, you kids have got taste.

steps.name: Timid Sick Child
steps.text: (Sobs uncontrollably)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Um...
Briefly at a loss, Lava rummages in her bag for a sweet to try and pacify the child, but then Hibiscus floats to mind, telling her children need to be on an empty stomach when testing their blood.
Screw her stupid sis! Dragging me out to help, saying these kids who just lost their parents in the war won't be that scared if they saw other Sarkaz. Well, they've been crying the whole time!
The relentless sobs throughout the ward leave her at a loss. For each and every day the war's still going, these cries will not come to an end.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Um... would you—like to see some fireworks?

steps.name: Timid Sick Child
steps.text: (Sobs)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I'll take that as a yes, then. Watch carefully, you only get to see them once.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: May my fires bring light to the lands!

A firework formed of flame leaps to the ceiling, and bursts in the air over the ward. Lava steals a sideways glance at the children's faces. The fiery display enraptures them, and for just the briefest moment they forget to cry.
Then, the flame sets off the fire systems, and everyone is doused in sprinkler water. For a while in the ward, just a fleeting while, laughter takes the place of cries.
Children are the same no matter where, it turns out. A flashy trick takes them in.
...Is it really the same? No matter where?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava, welcome back. How were the neighbors?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: The neighbors? I was just out to borrow some chili powder...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Do you feel alright after making the rounds? You didn't get into fights with anyone, did you?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I said I was just borrowing chili powder.

spans.text: I was just borrowing chili powder.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Lava? What are you looking for? Did you make new friends with the kids outside the door? You always were good with children—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Huh? Gone already? What's that... giant bag of things she took?

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Reporting in! The devil's left the house! She's now at the garden, over.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Whoa! Fire! Listen, the devil's using her flames... she just burned a log in half! Reporting in, the devil is building something massive out of a bunch of branches! Very suspicious!

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: What massive thing? Speak clearly!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: I can't tell! Reporting in, the devil's now airing out this giant white sheet... no, some kind of white witchcraft material, I bet, and she's draping it over the branches! Intelligence officer, analysis please!

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Intelligence officer here! Hmm, based on my view, this is definitely... some kind of dangerous altar.

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: That's right, the branches are holding up a screen. Look, she's rolling the log over now. It's an altar for putting offerings on.

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: (Gasp) The village is in danger!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: (Curls up)

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: C-Coward! We need to keep her under watch, and protect our village!

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Wait! She's brought something new out! Some kind of mechanical device, it looks like a... a projector? No, that can't be right! It must be a witchcraft casting device!
No sooner has she said it than the apparatus turns on, and upon the white 'witchcraft material' appears a roaring, skyscraper-dwarfing Feranmut.

steps.name: Children
steps.text: Eeeek—!
Boom! Bang!
In the scene projected on the 'material', a mutant Feranmut tramples high-rises into dust in an instant. The people wail and flee in despair, awaiting a hero to take the scene.
Lava, Rhodes Island elite operator, master caster, and Catastrophe expert. In this hour, any hope of the city surviving rests in her hands.

steps.name: Children
steps.text: Look! Someone's here to save the day!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: She's fighting that giant thing head on! Hold on, doesn't she look kind of like that devil...? No, she looks... exactly alike!
With a great swagger, Lava sits down on the children's so-called 'offerings altar' and kicks back, visibly enjoying the movie—
It wasn't any accident she brought this not-yet-released film along for the trip. She was meant to put a smile or two on her parents' faces with it.
For as much as she griped about the overdramatic plot being shoehorned in, it looks like the whole thing came together pretty damn well after all.
The children sneak glances at her, comparing her against the hero in the movie.
They can't understand any Yanese, but the special effects draw them in, and before they know it, they're inching closer, closer, until they're almost next to Lava herself.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Heh. Now I know you kids have taste, I can show you what real showtime looks like—)

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Oh no, the monster's going to flatten the building! Run, hero, run!

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Heroes don't run! Look! She's about to shoot fire at it!

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Hey... you two, where'd she go?

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Aaahhh, the monster's catching up!

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Hey! Hey! Sh—she's gone! That—whoever she was, that neighbor of ours...

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: What?! She was just sitting here! Where'd she go?
The spot where Lava was sat is, to everyone's surprise, now vacant. Suddenly, a ribbon of fire rolls forth, leaping out from behind them, running toward the bedsheet screen. The children shriek.

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Listen, this... this might be a real altar, I think! We got lured into it!

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Run... come on... Ah!
But the children stop running, as the spectacle before them stuns them into silence.

In front of their very eyes stands a woman in freshly garbed combat gear, the image of a hero in the billowing wind. With an elegant yet ruthless swish of the hand, flames catch hungrily upon the 'witchcraft material', a simple repurposed sheet.
The Feranmut on the screen howls in agony, and is burned to cinders. Thereupon the flames extinguish, not having touched a blade of the greenery about them.

steps.name: Children
steps.text: Whoaaa—

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: That was cool! Miss Hero, have you actually fought giant monsters like that?

steps.name: Theo
steps.text: Just now when you did that, right? Could you teach me that too?

steps.name: Rose
steps.text: Your battle clothes are so nice-looking! Like, they're so handsome!

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Miss Herooo, I asked first, so I get priority—argh! ...Mum?

The movie winds to a fiery close, and the children realize only then that their guardians have been watching all of them from close by with tense gazes. Now they approach, and each drags their respective child back home without even hearing an excuse.

steps.name: Ilsa's Mother
steps.text: Ilsa, I told you not to sneak off by yourself. You're grounded tonight. Think about what you've done.

steps.name: Ilsa
steps.text: Stop pulling, Mum! Listen, I got to see this really cool...

steps.name: Ilsa's Mother
steps.text: Not a word more.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: You don't have to run away, you know? It's not like I've got an extra pair of teeth or wings or anything compared to...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Whatever, leave me alone with my peace and quiet. No kids to entertain. They're just noisy little brats.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What's this...?
Where Ilsa sat, there quietly remains a bottle of chili powder. Lava stares blankly, then lifts her head and is about to shout a thank you after her, but they've all long vanished out of sight.
So, with nothing else to do, she picks it up and walks on home, a small and easy spring in her step.
